.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r15/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml (type/points of all 43 criteria tallied; ids listed; descriptions scanned for degree-of-quality wording, not each read in full)
evidence: Type tally over the five frozen judge.toml files: 55 criteria = 52 `type = "binary"` + 3 `type = "likert"` with `points = 5`. (1) Gates are binary only: tests/gates/render/judge.toml:20 and tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:20,29 are `type = "binary"`, as scoring.toml and the staged contract (staged-task-contract.md:96 'Gates stay at 0.0 and their criteria stay binary') require. (2) All 43 functional criteria are binary and are pass/fail behaviours with explicit fail conditions (e.g. cw_stale_save_refused, cw_time_limit_recovery); a scan for degree wording (smooth, comfortable, readable, polished, quality, mostly...) found none in functional/judge.toml, only timing tolerances such as 'within about ten seconds'. (3) The six polish criteria (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:20,29,38,47,56,65) are binary and each is an observable conjunction closed by 'Fails if ...' (keyboard reachability and visible focus, textual feedback after three actions, focus returning to the code, Undo/Redo disabled state, unsaved marker, 390 px usability); none asks for a degree of quality. This matches the frozen template, whose polish criteria are also binary. (4) The only craft / degree-of-quality criteria are the three visual ones and all are likert with points = 5 and an anchor written for every level 5,4,3,2,1,0: cw_visual_editor_readability (visual/judge.toml:20-21, anchors 25-30, e.g. '5: clear and comfortable throughout, numbers aligned, caret and selection easy to see.' ... '0: no editor is shown.'), cw_visual_workspace_layout (36-37, anchors 41-46) and cw_visual_component_finish (52-53, anchors 57-62). The 0..5 anchor shape with points = 5 is the same shape the frozen template visual/judge.toml ships (e.g. template lines 20-33). visual/prompt.md:9 tells the judge how to use them: 'Each criterion is scored from 0 to 5 using the anchors written in it. Those anchors take precedence over any generic 1 to 5 hint from the scoring tool. Apart from a failed global browser gate, 0 is used only when the thing being judged is not shown at all.' Per SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170 the internal workbook note that likert is not used is a known false positive; the check is whether craft is binary or anchors are missing, and neither occurs. Attempted counterexamples that did not hold: a plausible weak app (default browser styling, working features) lands on anchors 1-3 of the visual criteria and cannot collect full visual credit from a binary; a conforming alternative with an unusual palette is protected by visual/prompt.md 'Do not penalize the app's choice of hues as a matter of taste'; no behaviour criterion can be half-credited through a scale. NOTES (not defects): (a) the anchors for cw_visual_workspace_layout jump from '4: one or two small spacing issues.' / '3: several crowded or uneven areas.' to '2: frequent overlap or clipping.', so a single clipped or overlapping element has no named level and the judge must interpolate between 3 and 4; likewise cw_visual_editor_readability names 'numbers are misaligned' only at level 2, so a small misalignment in an otherwise clear editor sits ambiguously between 4 and 2. Bounded effect: one level on one of three criteria, about 0.013 of total reward. (b) How RewardKit normalises a judged 0 on a points = 5 likert is not measured for these bytes; the format is template-controlled and identical to the template, so it is not a task-authoring defect under this row. (c) Evidence check: of the artifacts listed in raw-evidence-index.json, the hosted-run result.json, reward.json and reward-details.json files and the scripted-golden scripts and result JSON/PNG files are not present at the indexed paths in this workspace at review time (only trial.log, app logs and a 43-byte scored/rewardkit.log under the hosted run, and build.log/restart.log under qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/results), so their hashes could not be verified and the indexed 'Visual 0.9167' figure is unverified by me. This row's verdict rests on the frozen rubric bytes, not on that evidence; no configured judge run exists for these bytes, so actual judge use of the anchors is not exercised. I did not recompute the snapshot input SHA256.
